LayoutEditor__KeyMappings__Description: Every mouse, wheel, keyboard and touch binding the Layout Editor listens for. Nothing in the control modules is hard-coded to a button or a key, so this file is the single place a binding changes. It is shaped to be handed to a user personalisation screen later: each binding carries an Id, a human Label and an Enabled flag, so a saved user override can be merged over the top of this file without the control code changing at all.
LayoutEditor__KeyMappings__Notes: Buttons are named Left, Middle and Right (mouse button 0, 1 and 2).
Modifiers are named Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Meta and Space. Space is the held space bar, tracked by the PC controls module.

ModifierMatch Exact means the listed modifiers must be the only ones held. ModifierMatch Any ignores modifiers entirely. ModifierMatch CoarseOptional means Exact, except that the coarse step modifier is allowed on top.
Bindings are tested in list order and the first enabled match wins, so put the more specific binding above the general one.
RequiresEmptyStage true limits a binding to a press that lands on the grey stage rather than on the paper.

Zoom limits and the wheel step live in Na__LayoutEditor__AppConfig__.json under LayoutEditor__Navigation__Config. This file owns which input triggers an action, that file owns how far and how fast it travels.

LayoutEditor__Guards__Config.LayoutEditor__Guards__Description: Elements inside the stage that keep their own input. A press or a wheel over one of these is left alone so a viewport canvas can drive its own camera and a panel control can be used.

LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__Config.LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__Descripti: Mouse and pen drags on the stage. The left button is deliberately left to the sheet tools unless a binding below claims it with a modifier or an empty-stage rule, which is the Lantern Designer rule: pan capture on a bare left button swallows the click before it reaches a dimension or a viewport.

LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__List.Label: Pan the sheet (middle or right drag)
LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__List.Note: Lantern Designer parity. This is the shipped default.

LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__List.Label: Pan the sheet (hold space, left drag)
LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__List.Note: The CAD and Illustrator convention. Left click still edits while space is up.

LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__List.Label: Pan the sheet (left drag on the grey stage)
LayoutEditor__PointerBindings__List.Note: Only fires when the press lands off the paper, so nothing on the sheet can be grabbed by accident.

LayoutEditor__WheelBindings__Config.LayoutEditor__WheelBindings__Description: What the wheel does over the stage. A trackpad reports a two-finger scroll as a wheel, so enabling the scroll bindings below and moving zoom onto Ctrl gives a laptop without a middle button a way to move around.

LayoutEditor__WheelBindings__List.Label: Zoom about the cursor
LayoutEditor__WheelBindings__List.Note: Lantern Designer parity. This is the shipped default.

LayoutEditor__WheelBindings__List.Label: Zoom about the cursor (ctrl held)
LayoutEditor__WheelBindings__List.Note: Pair this with the scroll bindings below and switch Zoom__Wheel off for trackpad behaviour.

LayoutEditor__WheelBindings__List.Label: Scroll the sheet up and down
Scroll the sheet left and right

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__Config.LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__Descript: Keys read while the editor is on screen. The navigation keys are shipped off so the bare arrow keys keep nudging the selection, which is the behaviour the editor already had. Switch them on here and the PC controls module picks them up with no code change. While the Draw or Dimension tool is placing a point the arrows lock the drawing axis instead of nudging, as in SketchUp LayOut; they go back to nudging the moment the point lands.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Pan left
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: Alt is held so this cannot collide with the selection nudge on the bare arrow keys.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Cancel placement, then clear the selection, then return to the select tool
Toggle object snapping to the linework (AutoCAD F3)
Undo the last change on the sheet
Copy the selected viewport
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: With no viewport selected the key is left to the browser, so copying text from a panel still works.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Paste the copied viewport as a new one: new id, new name, every setting kept
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: On the sheet it came from the paste steps clear of the original; on another sheet it lands in the same place.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Duplicate the selected viewport (copy and paste in one, the clipboard is left alone)
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: Taken from the browser while a sheet is open, where Ctrl+D would otherwise bookmark the page. Bare D is still the Dimension tool.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Clear the selection and abandon any placement (space bar)
Rectangle tool: draw a rectangle corner to corner
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: Click one corner then the opposite one, or drag from one to the other; Shift keeps it square. What it makes is an ordinary closed vector, so its corners are then dragged by their grips like any polygon's. Exact modifiers leave Ctrl+R to the browser.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Leader tool: a note or a specification bubble on a curved leader
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: Click the point the leader marks, then where its note or bubble goes - or drag from one to the other. The side of the point the head is placed on decides which way a note reads. The settings for new leaders are on the Leaders panel.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Nudge the selection left, or lock the X axis while a tool is placing a point
Nudge the selection right, or lock the X axis while a tool is placing a point
Nudge the selection up, or lock the Y axis while a tool is placing a point
Nudge the selection down, or lock the Y axis while a tool is placing a point
Eyedropper palette: use an object's style for new objects of its kind
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: Listed above plain B so the more specific binding is tested first, though Exact matching keeps the two apart anyway. Click an object and its style becomes the Text, Dimensions or Vectors setting that new objects are drawn with. Keep a scrapbook of one of each house style beside the paper, where it never prints.

LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Label: Eyedropper: match properties from one object onto another
LayoutEditor__KeyboardBindings__List.Note: B for Brush, as in the format painter every office application binds to the same idea. Click the object to copy from, then each object to copy onto; Alt+click picks a new source and Escape puts the dropper down.

LayoutEditor__TouchBindings__Config.LayoutEditor__TouchBindings__Description: Touch gestures on the stage. Two fingers always navigate, which is what keeps one finger free to select and drag the sheet contents. One finger also pans when it lands on the grey stage rather than on the paper, so there is always a way to move around without hunting for a spare button.

LayoutEditor__MeasurementsBox__Config.LayoutEditor__MeasurementsBox__Descripti: Typing into the Measurements box at the bottom right of the sheet, as in SketchUp: while the Draw, Rectangle or Dimension tool is up, a value typed anywhere over the editor goes into the box and Enter uses it, with no click into the box first. StartCharacters begin a value; letters are left to the tool keys until a value is begun. TypingCharacters are what a begun value may go on to hold: the digits, the point, the thousands comma, a sign, a space, the units (m, cm, mm) and the x, * or ; between a rectangle's width and height. A key outside them still reaches the sheet, and a tool key puts the value away. CommitKeys use the value, ClearKeys drop it and EraseKeys take its last character back - each only while something is typed, so Enter still finishes a shape and Escape still backs out while the box is empty. A text field, a select and any chord (Ctrl, Alt or Meta held) keep their keys. A click into the box types into it directly, which is also how a touch screen reaches it.

LayoutEditor__SelectionBindings__Config.LayoutEditor__SelectionBindings__Descrip: What a modifier held on a Select tool press does to the selection - for a click on an item and for a box dragged from bare paper alike - as SketchUp holds them. With none held the click or the box replaces the selection. The list is tested in order with Exact matching, so the two-modifier binding sits first. BoxAnywhereModifier is set aside before the list is tested: while it is held a drag draws a box even from on top of something that could be moved, which is the way in on a sheet with no bare paper left to start from, and Shift or Ctrl still combine with it. A box dragged to the right is a window (only what it wholly encloses); dragged to the left it is a crossing (anything it touches as well).

LayoutEditor__SelectionBindings__List.Label: Remove from the selection (Ctrl+Shift, click or box)
Add to the selection (Ctrl, click or box)
Add or remove, each item flipping (Shift, click or box)
LayoutEditor__SelectionBindings__List.Note: Shift held through a drag of the selection still keeps the move to one axis: an item only leaves the selection on a Shift click that did not move.

LayoutEditor__Actions__Config.LayoutEditor__Actions__Description: The action catalogue. A personalisation screen can read this to list what is bindable without knowing anything about the control modules.

LayoutEditor__Actions__List.Label: Add to or remove from the selection
